title: ARTIST Act

claims.sourceSpan: Section 101(b) of the Marine Mammal Protection Act Of 1972 (16 U.S.C. 1371(b)) is amended to read as follows
claims.claim: Rewrites the Alaska Native exemption in the Marine Mammal Protection Act

claims.sourceSpan: the taking of any marine mammal by any Alaska Native who resides in Alaska and who dwells on the coast of the North Pacific Ocean or the Arctic Ocean
claims.note: "coastal" = "dwells on the coast of the North Pacific Ocean or the Arctic Ocean"; "subsistence" = (2)(A)(i)(I) "is for subsistence purposes".
claims.claim: to protect the right of coastal Alaska Natives to harvest marine mammals for subsistence

claims.sourceSpan: is done for purposes of creating and selling authentic Alaska Native articles of handicrafts and clothing
claims.claim: and to make and sell authentic handicrafts

claims.sourceSpan: includes a tooth or tusk from a walrus (Odobenus rosmarus) or a species of cetacean
claims.note: Walrus verbatim. Source term is the broader "a species of cetacean"; "whale" is an in-scope lay subset (whale ivory items are covered) but under-inclusive vs the source (excludes e.g. narwhal/other cetaceans). Top_lines correctly says "cetacean". Minor imprecision, not contradictory.
claims.claim: including items made from walrus and whale ivory

claims.sourceSpan: No State shall prohibit the interstate commerce, importation, sale, offer for sale, transfer, trade, barter, possession, or possession with the intent to sell, transfer, trade, or barter of marine mammal ivory or marine mammal bone or baleen incorporated under this title by an Alaska Native, into an authentic Alaska Native article of handicrafts and clothing
claims.claim: It also bars states from blocking interstate sale of those handicrafts

notes: Source = enacted Public Law 119-99 text (S. 254, 6064 chars, read in full). One-section amendment: SEC. 2 replaces 16 U.S.C. 1371(b) (MMPA Alaska Native exemption) wholesale with a new (b)(1)-(5): definitions (authentic handicraft article, marine mammal ivory = walrus or cetacean tooth/tusk, traditional handicrafts), the subsistence + handicraft-creation/sale taking exemption (not wasteful; subject to section 109), interstate-commerce and edible-portion special rules, depletion-based regulation authority with notice/hearing + substantial-evidence (Native-brought-action) limits, a state-preemption prohibition, and a Tribal-rights rule of construction. Every substantive analysis claim is source-supported; 0 material issues. Minor flags: (1) 'public' hearing qualifier not in fetched text (section 103 not fetched); (2) 'several states restrict ivory sales' extrinsic context in underreported; (3) 'limited organized opposition' editorial framing in likelihoodReason; plus 3 minor omissions (rule of construction (5); the written/public-web-posting transparency mechanism in (3)(D); the 'Except as provided in section 109' carve-out). SUPPORTED-with-note imprecisions kept as baseline: summary 'whale ivory' narrows source 'a species of cetacean' (whale is an in-scope subset; top_lines correctly says 'cetacean'); top_lines 'Defines...as' vs source 'includes'; edible-portion top_line compresses the source disjunction (section detail states it correctly). featured_quotes (Westerman W000821, Begich B001323, Sullivan S001198) are Congressional-Record floor statements NOT present in this enacted-law source file and no referencedSources were registered — not auditable against source; not flagged as fabrication. No divisions[]. changes[] novelty ('New' bar / new definitions) vs pre-amendment 1371(b) not independently verifiable (prior-edition statute not fetched); substance fully present in enacted text.
